## Reproduced at `b06cfa5a6f7977f3d86c6c349c8fd1ce48a7bf05`

[`test/fixtures.ts:31–35`](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-jev/blob/b06cfa5a6f7977f3d86c6c349c8fd1ce48a7bf05/test/fixtures.ts#L31-L35) creates a temporary child directory, then passes `resolveImplicitPmRoot(cwd)` to `PmClient.init`. The [existing fixture goal](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-jev/blob/b06cfa5a6f7977f3d86c6c349c8fd1ce48a7bf05/.agents/pm/features/pm-jev-0q58.toon) is a fresh isolated tracker, even with inherited configuration. This is distinct from its covered `PM_PATH` override.

Using Linux, Node 24.22.1, Git 2.52.0 and locked npm PM CLI 2026.11.14, I created a disposable Git repository `outer` and a `jev-test-*` child inside it. With the helper's exact resolution/init sequence, the SDK created `outer/.agents/pm/settings.json`; no tracker was initialized in the child. With a tracker already initialized in `outer`, the same sequence refused without `--force`. No real checkout or provider was touched. The SDK is performing its intended ancestor discovery; the test fixture's assumption is the defect, and it is not attributed to the dependency bump.

In a marked temporary parent, the pristine focused agent-UX and evaluation suites passed 4/21 (17 setup failures). In the isolated copy, changing only the fixture to explicitly own its child tracker root restored 21/21; production source was unchanged.

## Acceptance
- Place `TMPDIR` inside disposable Git parents both with and without an initialized tracker. The helper creates and removes only its own child tracker; the initialized parent stays byte-identical and the empty parent remains tracker-free.
- Retain the existing inherited-`PM_PATH` regression and run the focused agent-UX/evaluation tests. Do not change SDK implicit discovery or loosen overwrite protection to make the tests pass.
Test fixture can initialize its enclosing Git checkout instead of its own temporary tracker
